newsitem.title: FRANCE: UN's Chretien in France to meet Zaire's Mobutu.
newsitem.headline: UN's Chretien in France to meet Zaire's Mobutu.

text.p: Raymond Chretien, the U.N. envoy for the crisis in eastern Zaire, has arrived in France for talks on Wednesday with ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko at the Zairean leader's Riviera retreat.

"The aim of my visit is to meet President Mobutu who has agreed to receive me," Chretien told reporters late on Tuesday night after his flight to Nice airport. He said he planned to meet Mobutu on Wednesday afternoon.

He said Mobutu, resting in a luxury personal mansion overlooking the Mediterranean for a few days before returning to his troubled nation, had been the "guarantor of the security of his country for many decades".

"I come to meet him and benefit from his advice in a completely open spirit with no prejudices," Chretien said. He said Mobutu "has been an active president who was always in control when he was in Kinshasa".

Chretien, Canada's ambassador to the United States, said he planned to hold a news conference after his talks with Mobutu and before flying to Kinshasa for talks with Zairean Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo.

Mobutu arrived in France on Monday from Switzerland for a few days' stay at his pink and white marble villa at Roquebrun-Cap-Martin near Nice after undergoing surgery for prostate cancer in Lausanne in August.
He has remained silent since fighting broke out in his country between Zairean troops and Rwandan-backed Tutsi rebels that has trapped more than one million starving refugees.

At a summit in Nairobi on Tuesday, eight African nations urged the United Nations to arrange a "neutral" protection force to come to the rescue of a million abandoned refugees in Zaire, but volunteers for the force appeared sparse.

French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette on Wednesday reiterated France's plan to send international force to help ensure that refugees and others displaced by the fighting can get food and supplies. He said that there was six months' food within 1,000 km (625 miles) of the refugee camps.
